newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh Islamists call for strike over defamation.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh Islamists call for strike over defamation.

text.p: Leading Islamic groups in Bangladesh have called for a countrywide general strike on Tuesday to protest against what they regard as attempts to "ridicule and defame" the Prophet Mohammad.
"The strike is intended to voice our strongest protest against attempts to ridicule the Prophet by blasphemous acts of an Israeli Jewish woman," said Abdul Quader Mollah of the Jamaat-e-Islami party.

Religious feelings were inflamed in Bangladesh, where nearly 90 percent of its 120 million people are Moslems, after a right-wing Jewish woman in Hebron plastered storefronts two weeks ago with posters portraying Mohammed as a pig.
"True Moslems can never tolerate the outrageous act and the devilish courage to dishonour (Prophet) Mohammad," said a leader of the radical Islamic Constitution Movement.
"The strike would reflect our anger ... and whip up conscientiousness across the world," the Islami Oikya Jote, an Islamic council, said in a statement.
Moslems feelings were also hurt after Palestinians said Israeli troops ransacked the al-Yaacoubia school and tore up copies of the Koran.
The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the Jatiya Party of former military ruler Hossain Mohammad Ershad backed the proposed strike.
"We support Tuesday's hartal (strike) because any act against the Prophet and Islam calls for unanimous indignation and protest," BNP secretary-general Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan said.
The Jatiya Party said it supported the strike to "show respect to people's sentiment."
The ruling Awami League opposes the planned dawn-to-dusk strike, saying that it is unwarranted after the Bangladesh parliament adopted a unanimous resolution condemning the blasphemy.
Awami leader Amir Hossain Amu said the proponents of the strike had other motives to pursue under a pro-Islamic cover.

The government has strongly protested and expressed its indignation "against the dastardly acts of the Jews designed to defame our Prophet and the holy Koran," he said in a statement published in newspapers on Monday.
The strike could hit transport, business and all administrative functions in the country.
